topic: Honest-width frontier for horizon-adaptive nested donor pools in staggered synthetic controls. Fix finite treated units and horizons, deterministic adoption dates, observed predictors x_i, and deduplicated unit-calendar-time untreated outcomes with conditional means m_it=x_i' beta_t+r_it, ||beta_t||<=L, |r_it|<=delta/2, and known Gaussian covariance Sigma_Q with eigenvalues in a fixed positive band. For each treated j and horizon h let D_jh={i:T_i>T_j+h}. Among deterministic linear-SC rectangular bands whose weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design/model inputs, define W_nested by horizon-specific support D_jh and W_deep by common support D_jK, under uniform joint 1-alpha coverage. Characterize W_nested up to universal constants using a fixed-Bonferroni bias-plus-standard-error SOCP, prove a matching lower bound and finite-sample coverage, prove W_nested<=W_deep, and give a necessary-and-sufficient primal-dual certificate for strict improvement valid on degenerate active faces. Treat correlated Gaussian-max calibration only as a post-solve refinement. Consumers are scpi and augsynth::multisynth. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The prediction error was derived as one observable worst-case bias radius plus a Gaussian contrast on the deduplicated unit–calendar-time vector. With a fixed Bonferroni multiplier, minimizing the maximum bias-plus-standard-error envelope under simplex and nested-support constraints is a genuine SOCP with finite-sample simultaneous coverage; correlated Gaussian-max calibration is only a post-solve refinement. Each contrast retains a unique treated coordinate, so its contrast Gram matrix is at least the identity and the covariance is uniformly bounded below by sigma_min. Together with coordinatewise attainable bias shifts and an Anderson Gaussian-cube bound, this yields a finite constant-factor comparison between the SOCP envelope and exact robust width, subject to formal verification. Nested feasible-set inclusion proves width cannot worsen. In the two-horizon witness, optimized early nested weights (50/51,1/102,1/102) give variance 101/5100 versus 51/100 for deepest-pool support, with common second-horizon variance 3/200; exact 95% simultaneous full widths were computed as 0.593131 versus 2.799389. No collision was found with CFPT, partially pooled staggered synthetic controls, scpi/multisynth, or Cao–Lu–Wu. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a necessary-and-sufficient nested-primal/deep-dual strict-gap certificate that remains valid on degenerate active faces, using relative-interior strong duality and interval-certified positive gaps. EARLY KILL TEST: Formalize the covariance-domination/Anderson sandwich and the finite Gaussian-quantile ratio bound; pivot if any legal deduplicated design with fixed eigenvalue bounds violates either inequality or makes the ratio diverge.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax worst-coordinate half-width of a uniformly honest simultaneous rectangular band when each treated-unit–horizon contrast may use its full not-yet-treated donor set D_jh, and is a fixed-Bonferroni worst-case-bias-plus-standard-error SOCP optimal up to constants among deterministic linear synthetic-control bands?

source_refs.claim: The paper defines event-time-varying donor sets but uses the deepest-horizon set D_jK to avoid spurious changes from donor composition, while noting that the estimator need not impose this restriction.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, Avi Feller, and Jesse Rothstein
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: The paper gives non-asymptotic prediction intervals, conic implementations, and simultaneous inference for staggered synthetic controls, but no minimum-width characterization over horizon-varying donor supports.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Filippo Palomba, and Rocio Titiunik

source_refs.claim: The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and efficiency bounds for scalar linear functionals over convex regression classes under Gaussian errors with known variance.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong and Michal Kolesár

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein isolate the donor-support tension but optimize pre-treatment balance rather than honest joint width; CFPT supply non-asymptotic joint prediction intervals and conic computation without solving the decision problem over horizon-specific supports. Armstrong–Kolesár's scalar modulus argument does not directly yield a lower bound for a Gaussian rectangle whose coordinates lie on different nested simplex faces. The missing step is a simultaneous lower bound that couples coordinatewise attainable bias shifts with the covariance geometry of all deduplicated treated-unit–horizon contrasts; searches for horizon-specific donors, nested donor pools, and bias-variance SOCP bands found no such frontier theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample upper-and-lower characterization, up to constants for fixed alpha and covariance eigenvalue band, of the optimal maximum half-width, together with an explicit bias-plus-standard-error SOCP and a uniform simultaneous 1-alpha coverage theorem.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation isolates the changing donor-set problem and explains why the conventional deepest-pool restriction is attractive despite discarding valid early donors.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered adoption creates event-time-specific untreated sets -> deepest-horizon pools avoid compositional artifacts but discard valid early donors -> honest inference should characterize the attainable width gain from nested sets

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the convex-class modulus and known-variance Gaussian proof that turns worst-case bias and standard deviation into an honest fixed-length interval and minimax lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each synthetic-control error is likewise a linear functional over a convex bounded-mean class, but the scalar modulus must be lifted to a finite Gaussian maximum.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their synthetic-control prediction-error decomposition, conic reformulation, and maximal-inequality proof of simultaneous coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already handles staggered adoption, constrained synthetic-control weights, and joint post-treatment inference; the new object changes the weight objective and support geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the dual-norm representation of conditional worst-case bias and the convex optimization trading squared imbalance against residual variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed SOCP has the same bias-versus-variance geometry, with simplex donor restrictions and a maximum across causal contrasts replacing one balancing estimand.

open_problems.open_problem: What necessary-and-sufficient primal-dual condition characterizes strict reduction of optimized honest width from deepest-pool support D_jK to nested supports D_jh when the optimum lies on a degenerate simplex or second-order-cone face?

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly contrasts event-time-varying donor sets D_jh with the fixed deepest-horizon pool D_jK, but does not characterize when the restriction is strictly costly.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, Avi Feller, and Jesse Rothstein
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Its conic uncertainty-quantification framework supplies the relevant optimization geometry but does not give an exact strict-gap comparison on degenerate active faces.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Filippo Palomba, and Rocio Titiunik

source_refs.excerpt: projection computation, and zero-test convention under singular Schur blocks.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Feasible-set inclusion proves only weak improvement. Ordinary KKT or Slater arguments can fail when zero weights, tight variance cones, or redundant donor columns put the optimizer on a lower-dimensional face; the adjacent panel_sdid_mc_id review independently demanded a zero-test that remains valid under singular Schur blocks. Thus a certificate based on one selected optimizer or multiplier is not necessary under nonuniqueness. The missing step is to restrict both conic programs to their minimal faces, establish relative-interior strong duality and dual attainment there, and prove that a positive nested-primal versus deep-dual gap is equivalent to strict value improvement rather than merely sufficient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff certificate consisting of a feasible nested-support primal point and an attained deepest-pool relative-interior dual point with an interval-certified positive objective gap, plus an equality characterization valid on every minimal active face.

writing_exemplar.why: Its fixed-versus-changing donor-pool discussion frames the applied question of when the simplifying restriction actually costs precision.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed D_jK stabilizes event-time composition -> nested D_jh enlarges feasible weight sets -> practitioners need a checkable condition for when that enlargement yields a genuine precision gain

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the robust conic representation of synthetic-control uncertainty, then derive exact primal and dual programs for the maximum-width objective.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate compares two support-restricted versions of the same causal-band conic program.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply closed-cone Farkas alternatives and strong-duality conditions after restricting each SOCP to its minimal face.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses the dual-attainment failure that makes a naive strict-gap test incomplete on degenerate faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Use facial reduction to construct an exact strong dual when standard conic constraint qualifications fail.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Zero donor weights and redundant balance equations create the lower-dimensional cone geometry for which facial reduction supplies complete certificates.

open_problems.open_problem: Under fixed positive lower and upper eigenvalue bounds for the deduplicated Gaussian outcome covariance, is the fixed-Bonferroni nested-donor SOCP uniformly within a finite constant factor of the optimally correlation-calibrated robust rectangular-band width, or can the ratio diverge with the number and geometry of contrasts?

source_refs.claim: For simultaneous post-treatment prediction the paper uses a maximal sub-Gaussian bound and notes that alternative simultaneous strategies are more computationally demanding and require stronger conditions.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Filippo Palomba, and Rocio Titiunik

source_refs.claim: The paper proves explicit comparison and anti-concentration bounds for maxima of Gaussian vectors with general covariance matrices.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, and Kengo Kato

source_refs.claim: Anderson's inequality compares Gaussian probability content of translated symmetric convex sets and is the classical bridge from covariance domination to rectangle-probability bounds.
source_refs.author: T. W. Anderson
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society

source_refs.excerpt: the Gaussian maximum benchmark is not minimax.
quantify the cost of shared-cell correlation relative to a diagonal approximation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: CFPT's generic maximal calibration is valid without exploiting the full correlation structure, while exact Gaussian-max calibration depends on the entire weight-induced contrast covariance. Raw-outcome eigenvalue bounds do not immediately control the quantile ratio after the contrast rows themselves are optimized and share treated and donor cells. The prior close-group writeup further warns that a Gaussian maximum benchmark need not be minimax in an adjacent donor-face problem, so exact maximum inversion cannot simply be declared the lower benchmark. The missing step is an Anderson covariance sandwich plus a dimension-uniform finite Gaussian-quantile comparison after coordinatewise bias shifts, or a legal deduplicated design showing that one of those comparisons fails.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a dimension-uniform inequality W_Bonferroni <= C(alpha, covariance band) W_exact with a matching lower example, or a legal sequence of deduplicated staggered designs satisfying the eigenvalue bounds for which W_Bonferroni/W_exact diverges.

writing_exemplar.why: Its simultaneous-inference discussion explains why simple maximal calibrations are implementable and why correlation-aware alternatives may be sharper but harder.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Joint post-treatment coverage is required -> maximal inequalities provide a simple valid calibration -> determine whether correlation-aware calibration can improve honest nested-donor width by more than a constant factor

method_exemplars.technique: Use covariance-sensitive Gaussian-max comparison and anti-concentration to convert covariance perturbations into explicit quantile perturbations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact robust calibration is the quantile of a finite maximum of correlated Gaussian synthetic-control contrasts.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gaussian covariance domination to centered hyperrectangles and combine it with attainable coordinatewise mean shifts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A simultaneous rectangular band is a symmetric convex Gaussian acceptance set, making Anderson's inequality the natural coverage comparison.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt biased-Gaussian critical-value calculations and honest-efficiency comparisons from one statistic to a maximum of shifted correlated coordinates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems ask how worst-case bias and Gaussian standard error force interval width; the new ingredient is simultaneous correlation geometry.

open_problems.open_problem: Can horizon-adaptive nested-donor synthetic-control bands remain uniformly honest and constant-factor width-optimal when the Gaussian covariance is unknown and must be estimated under serial or cluster dependence with unit–calendar-time cells reused across horizons?

source_refs.excerpt: Develop a serially dependent or clustered-error extension with a valid covariance estimator
Covariance consistency is likewise not established, because the theorem stops at a deterministic implication

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known-covariance Gaussian reduction removes the main feasible-inference difficulty. Under serial or cluster dependence, the same donor and treated cells enter several horizon contrasts, and optimized weights depend nonsmoothly on the plug-in covariance. The banked MNAR run recorded the same shared-cell bookkeeping problem and explicitly failed to establish covariance consistency. The missing first step is a dependence-robust covariance estimator with a uniform rate strong enough to stabilize the random SOCP solution and its induced contrast Gram matrix; without it, neither simultaneous coverage nor the constant-factor width comparison transfers.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A feasible covariance estimator and plug-in nested-support SOCP with a uniform simultaneous-coverage theorem and a constant-factor expected-width or oracle-width comparison over an explicit serially dependent or clustered panel class.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates uncertainty from weight construction and post-treatment prediction, the right narrative for adding covariance learning to a bias-aware band.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic-control prediction uses fitted weights -> fitting and post-period noise create distinct uncertainty -> valid intervals must propagate both -> add dependent covariance learning while retaining horizon-adaptive donor optimization

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate exact cellwise influence coefficients, retain reused-cell covariance products, and construct a heteroskedastic feasible variance estimate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination likewise has horizon contrasts sharing untreated cells; the new proof must add serial dependence and SOCP-selected coefficients.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine Gaussian comparison, covariance replacement, anti-concentration, and multiplier calibration for maxima of correlated sums.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Uniform coverage across treated-unit horizons is a correlated maximum problem after the plug-in contrast map is stabilized.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the finite-sample honest-width frontier when each horizon's nested donor support is selected from noisy pre-treatment closeness scores with root-sample local separations, and can a support selector attain an oracle inequality relative to the best deterministic nested-support band?

source_refs.claim: The paper treats initial donor count as a bias-variance complexity parameter and proposes pre-treatment cross-validated forward selection to improve out-of-sample prediction.
source_refs.author: Giovanni Cerulli

source_refs.claim: The paper gives data-driven tuning and joint prediction intervals for constrained synthetic controls while treating admissible horizon-specific donor sets as supplied rather than selected model classes.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, Filippo Palomba, and Rocio Titiunik

source_refs.excerpt: the genuinely noisy sqrt(n)-scaled local experiment, but it needs a new proposal.
The exact finite frontier concerns the bounded-spread score-only experiment

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cerulli's selector targets prediction RMSPE for one synthetic-control exercise, whereas the relevant loss is the largest honest bias-aware half-width over a staggered event-study family. CFPT's joint inference does not supply an oracle theorem for selecting the support pattern. The failed close-group run shows why a fixed-support proof cannot simply be conditioned on the selected set: exact score observation changes the local experiment, while actual donor scores and effects remain jointly noisy and near-ties generate unions of active simplex faces. The missing first step is therefore a legal joint score-and-effect local experiment, followed by sample splitting or a Gaussian-process argument uniform over candidate nested support patterns.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A declared noisy-score parameter class and support-selection rule with uniform 1-alpha simultaneous coverage plus a finite-sample excess-width oracle bound, or an impossibility theorem identifying the precise separation or spread regime in which every honest procedure has infinite or non-oracle width.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames donor-pool size as a genuine bias-variance tuning problem and motivates restriction by out-of-sample performance.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Using every donor can overfit -> donor-pool size is selected from pre-treatment data -> staggered applications need selection aimed at honest joint width rather than prediction RMSPE

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Gaussian anti-concentration and multiplier critical values that remain honest after data-dependent resolution selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Selecting a donor-support pattern is structurally analogous to selecting a resolution level before reporting a supremum-norm confidence band.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the staggered synthetic-control error decomposition and joint calibration, made uniform over a finite support class or combined with sample splitting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest causal predictands, constraints, and simultaneous-coverage argument; random support choice is the additional obstacle.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the noisy-selection Gaussian experiment and projection-versus-length comparison to derive honest post-selection inference near local ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Root-sample donor-score separation creates the same nonregular selection geometry, now replicated across nested horizons.

literature_map:
Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, JRSSB, arXiv:1912.03290) is the closest donor-pool anchor: D_jh varies with horizon, but the paper uses D_jK to avoid event-time compositional changes.
The same paper introduces partially pooled weights balancing unit-specific and pooled pre-treatment fit; augsynth::multisynth implements the estimator.
Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, ReStat, arXiv:2210.05026) is the closest inference anchor: non-asymptotic staggered-SC prediction intervals, conic computation, and simultaneous post-treatment inference.
CFPT's simultaneous out-of-sample analysis uses a maximal sub-Gaussian calibration and describes sharper alternatives as more computationally demanding.
CFPT also notes that not-yet-treated donors create special conditioning issues because their features and outcomes can enter multiple components.
Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021, JASA, arXiv:1912.07120) supplies the single-treated prediction-error decomposition inherited by CFPT.
Cattaneo et al. (2025, JSS, arXiv:2202.05984) documents scpi's simultaneous intervals and simplex/L1/L2 estimators but does not optimize width over horizon-varying supports.
Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1912.06320) use not-yet-treated units with long-preperiod asymptotics rather than finite-sample minimax width.
Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens, and Wager (2021, AER, DOI:10.1257/aer.20190159) provide the synthetic-DiD benchmark for weighted panel estimators.
Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2021, JASA, arXiv:1811.04170) and Abadie–L'Hour (2021, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2021.1971535) address imperfect fit and penalization, not nested-support honest-width frontiers.
Chernozhukov, Wüthrich, and Zhu (2021, JASA, arXiv:1712.09089) and Li (2020, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2019.1686986) give alternative conformal and long-panel inference regimes.
Armstrong–Kolesár (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1511.06028; 2020, QE, arXiv:1606.01200) provide the closest honest bias-aware efficiency machinery, but for scalar linear functionals.
Kallus (2020, JMLR, arXiv:1612.08321) casts balancing weights as worst-case bias-variance optimization, the closest optimization analogy.
Cerulli (2024, Economics Letters, DOI:10.1016/j.econlet.2024.111976) makes donor count a cross-validated complexity parameter without staggered simultaneous honest inference.
Chernozhukov–Chetverikov–Kato (2014, AoS, arXiv:1303.7152; 2015, PTRF, arXiv:1301.4807) and Anderson (1955) supply adaptive-band, Gaussian-max, anti-concentration, and covariance-domination tools.
